BiblicalUsage: Bazah means to despise, to disesteem, to count as nothing. Esau despises his birthright for a bowl of pottage, Goliath disdains David when he sees he is only a youth, Isaiah says the Servant is despised and rejected of men, and Malachi says the priests despise God's name while they offer polluted bread on His altar.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe despising is the sin that looks smallest and costs the most, because Esau sold his birthright for a meal and the priests sold God's honour for convenience. The Servant was despised and rejected, and I hold that the God men despise is the God who saves them.
